transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-21 | Start: 16:00 PST | Duration: 47m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Torres (PenumbraAI - Head of ML), Rafael Gomez (PenumbraAI - Platform Engineer), Priya Shah (PenumbraAI - FinOps)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick mic check?
[00:05] Lina Torres: Sounds good from my side.
[00:07] Rafael Gomez: Yup, can hear you.
[00:09] Maya Chen: Great. I'm Maya, I'll run the intro, and Owen will walk through the console and route-level cost stuff. We're aiming to focus on your FinOps questions and the per-route dashboards.
[00:20] Owen Patel: Hi all, quick agenda: 1) high-level Console tour, 2) per-route usage & cost breakdown, 3) Optimize suggestions (batching/caching/quant), 4) Q&A + pilot next steps.
[00:33] Priya Shah: Sounds perfect. Our main asks are: predictable spend, route-level chargeback, and visibility for model degeneration alerts.
[00:45] Owen Patel: Got it. We'll demo a real account view and then show how you can map your routes to internal cost centers.

-- Demo start --
[01:10] Owen Patel: (screen share) Alright this is the Console landing, top-left you can pick time ranges and route filters. The main idea: every route is an entity with metrics for calls, tokens in/out, latency p50/p95, and cost attribution.
[01:35] Lina Torres: Do you map by path or by model endpoint? We have a handful of internal microservices hitting the API.
[01:42] Owen Patel: Both. You can tag routes via SDK headers or in the Console because we ingest route name and group it. For microservices you can auto-map by service name header.
[02:05] Rafael Gomez: What's the sampling window for latency? We care about p99 under burst.
[02:10] Owen Patel: Default is continuous 1-minute aggregation with 1s granularity for traces. p99 is available; we also show distribution histograms. During heavy bursts the Console will surface autoscaling events and queueing metrics.

[03:00] Speaker 1: (background) -- sorry, go ahead.

[03:12] Owen Patel: Example route: "search-summarize". Here you can see token mix — prompt vs completion — and the cost per million tokens attributed to that route. We apply model-specific unit pricing and any caching/batching discounts.
[03:40] Priya Shah: Can you show a real cost breakdown for a month? We need to understand what a predictable commit would look like.
[03:50] Owen Patel: Sure. (navigates) Here's a 30-day view. Left: raw spend by route. Middle: normalized cost per 1k calls. Right: suggested optimizations. You can click a route and see the top contributing endpoints and the sequence length distribution which influences kernel selection and cost.
[04:20] Lina Torres: Sequence length distribution — that's really useful. We have a few outliers with 4k tokens that drive cost.
[04:28] Owen Patel: Yep, you can set SLO alerts on heavy tails and enforce truncation or model fallbacks.

[05:05] Maya Chen: Quick question on billing model: if we move to Dedicated, how does the per-route view change? Does the Console still surface per-route cost?
[05:13] Owen Patel: Yes. For Dedicated you'll see capacity amortized across routes; the Console will show both marginal token cost and amortized infra cost. There's a toggle to look at pure token spend vs total unit economics including reserved GPU amortization.
[05:40] Rafael Gomez: That amortization math — can we export it? We want to feed this into our internal chargeback tool.
[05:45] Owen Patel: Absolutely. Exports available: CSV and a S3 dump. We'll include route_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_version, batch settings, quant profile.

[06:25] Priya Shah: On security — SOC2, KMS, VPC — we need to know data flows for private deployment. Who handles keys?
[06:33] Maya Chen: We support customer-managed KMS and HSM for Private; logs are shipped to your SIEM and audit logs are retained per the enterprise package. I can share the SOC2 and KMS integration docs after the call.
[06:50] Lina Torres: Is there an on-prem option? We need an air-gapped test for PHI later.
[06:55] Owen Patel: Yes, we have a Private on-prem appliance and a VPC option. Note: on-prem has a heavier ops onboarding but we support it for regulated workloads.

[07:30] Owen Patel: Back to the Console — here's route drill-down. Top is throughput chart, below is token density heatmap. You can see that at 11/9 we had a spike where average seq length doubled. That spike corresponded with a 3x cost bump.
[07:55] Rafael Gomez: That spike — do you keep the raw request payloads? We usually anonymize but want the shape.
[08:00] Owen Patel: We keep telemetry (lengths, headers, model chosen), not raw user text unless you opt-in for debug traces; there's a redact feature and PII scrubber.

[08:30] Owen Patel: Now, Optimize tab — this is where we run heuristics and model recommendations. Example: route "answers-fast" has low quality tolerance but is high volume, we recommend batching at 64 tokens and enabling prefix KV caching for templated prompts. The expected cost reduction is shown (about 28% here).
[09:05] Priya Shah: How reliable are those estimates? We need conservative numbers for finance.
[09:10] Owen Patel: Estimates are based on empirical traces — we replay a sampled window against suggested config in a simulation environment. It reports delta in tokens, expected latency change, and unit cost. We surface a confidence band. It's not a guarantee but historically within 5-12% of actuals.
[09:45] Lina Torres: Is quantization suggested automatically? We care about quality drop.
[09:50] Owen Patel: Yes, Optimize will recommend quant profiles per model per route, and provide A/B test harness to measure regen/quality impact.

[10:30] Speaker 2: (interrupt) are there any built in fallbacks for model unavailability?
[10:34] Owen Patel: Yes, Smart routing policies let you set fallbacks by latency or cost tier — you can route to a cheaper quantized variant under pressure. It logs when fallbacks occur so ops can monitor degradation.

[11:15] Priya Shah: About chargeback — can we create custom cost buckets? We have product lines and cost centers.
[11:20] Owen Patel: You can define cost buckets and mapping rules (route name prefix, header tag, or regex). The Console then rolls up spend into those buckets and produces an export for billing.

[12:05] Maya Chen: Quick demo of Alerts — you can set route-level budget thresholds and SLO-based alerts that tie into PagerDuty/Slack.
[12:20] Owen Patel: Also an anomaly detector that surfaces spend drift vs baseline with suggested root causes (model change, seq length, traffic shift).

[13:00] Rafael Gomez: For the pilot, we'd like to run a 2-hour throughput benchmark on our representative routes. We'll want to validate latencies at p95 and throughput at steady state.
[13:10] Owen Patel: Perfect — we can run that in Dedicated sandbox or in your VPC with Private control plane. For quickness, the Dedicated sandbox is easiest.

[14:05] Lina Torres: Any gotchas on billing during the pilot? We don't want surprises.
[14:10] Maya Chen: Pilots are meter-based; we'll provide expected spend range and commit thresholds. We'll put a spend cap and send alerts before the cap is hit.

[15:00] Owen Patel: Demoing a shared artifact — here's a sample CSV export we mentioned. (shows file) It has per-request aggregates zipped by minute, includes model, tokens, time, route_id. You can drop into your cost model or FinOps tooling.
[15:28] Priya Shah: Nice. Can you also include the reserved vs variable split in the CSV?
[15:33] Owen Patel: Yes, we can include columns for reserved_capacity_allocation and marginal_cost.

[16:00] Lina Torres: On the product side — how fast do model rollouts happen? We have an internal process for canaries.
[16:06] Owen Patel: Console supports canary rollouts by percent and A/B comparisons on quality and cost. There's automatic rollback if quality regression is detected against a baseline prompt set.

[17:00] Rafael Gomez: For telemetry ingestion — what's the retention window? We need 13 months for audits.
[17:05] Maya Chen: Enterprise retention can be extended; standard is 90 days but with enterprise add-on you can get 13 months plus long-term cold storage exports.

[18:10] Owen Patel: Quick pause — any other pressing questions?
[18:18] Priya Shah: One last on forecasting: can we forecast next quarter spend given current route growth?
[18:25] Owen Patel: There's a forecasting model that extrapolates by route with seasonality and growth rates; it also provides uncertainty bands. You can export forecast to CSV.

-- Wrap & Recap --
[20:00] Maya Chen: To recap: We'll send SOC2 and private deployment checklist, Owen will share the sample CSV and a starter dashboard, and Penumbra will provide traffic patterns for the pilot. We agreed on a 2-hour benchmark kickoff week of 11/30.
[20:25] Lina Torres: That works. Also can we get a short doc on how you calculate amortized reserved costs? Rafael will need that.
[20:34] Maya Chen: Yes, I'll include the reserved math in the pricing template.

[21:00] Priya Shah: Thanks, this was useful.
[21:05] Rafael Gomez: Appreciate the transparency. We'll take the exported sample and start mapping to our cost centers.
[21:12] Owen Patel: I'll follow up with the CSV and a link to a pre-baked dashboard you can clone.
[21:20] Maya Chen: Great. I'll also drop the SOC2 pack and KMS notes.
[21:26] Lina Torres: Thanks everyone.
[21:30] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up by Thursday.

Notes: audio had occasional overlap, some product names transcribed as "KV cash" or "serve runtime" misread. References: Console deck: https://redwood.app/decks/penumbra-console.pdf | Sample CSV export link (mock): https://redwood.app/exports/penumbra-sample.csv

End of transcript.
